 Papillion couple waits 8 months for federal tax refund 
 As the cost of living goes higher, so does the frustration of a Papillion couple. They could use money that the federal government owes them. By Mike McKnight Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 10:28 PM CST | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google OMAHA, Neb. (WOWT) - As the cost of living goes higher, so does the frustration of a Papillion couple. They could use money that the federal government owes them.
 For about eight months, Rosie Kircher has walked to the mailbox hoping this will be the day.
 “I keep looking for the IRS letter. But there’s no check once again,” Rosie Kircher said.
 The Kirchers say they received their Nebraska income tax refund within three weeks of filing in March. But they claim the IRS has yet to send or deposit their federal refund of $11,255.
 “We have that much money sitting somewhere that we could be using or doing something with, and it’s just sitting there, and what is the government doing with it?” Tom Kircher said.
 Automated message says return is under review
 When the IRS phone line was called, an automated message said, “We’ve received your tax return and it is being reviewed.”
 The IRS has said the review would take 60 days. The couple says they have received that notice three times and are now about eight months in.
 Asked how frustrating it is when the IRS says the return is under review but does not say why, Tom Kircher said, “It’s very frustrating. Let me know if you need something else and we’ll get it to you.”
 The couple says they have been able to reach only a recorded attendant, not a real IRS representative, to ask why their refund has not been sent in eight months.
 “I have to go to the grocery store just like everybody else. I have to go to the gas station, and the prices keep going up,” Rosie Kircher said.
 Website offered advice for a fee
 Tom Kircher looked for answers on what he thought was an IRS website, which offered advice for $65.
 “But the IRS doesn’t run a chat service with star ratings and a sales pitch. If it’s not irs.gov, it’s not the IRS,” said Josh Planos of the Better Business Bureau.
 Almost every day, the retirees check their bank account for an automatic deposit and their mailbox for a check. Either way, they say the IRS has not responded.
 “No check,” Rosie Kircher said.
 The tax advice website appears to be associated with the government. Tom Kircher received an alert from his bank, which stopped the credit card charge.
 After numerous emails, the IRS has not responded to a request for comment.
